understand.restatement: Given a list nums of nonnegative integers, choose elements with no two chosen positions adjacent. Return the largest possible sum. You may choose none, and empty lists return 0.
understand.outputs: The maximum sum of nonadjacent elements.
constraints: Given a list nums of nonnegative integers, choose elements with no two chosen positions adjacent. Return the largest possible sum. You may choose none, and empty lists return 0.

examples.explanation: Choosing 2, 9, and 1 gives the maximum sum 12.
This boundary case follows the stated input and output rules.

pattern.name: Dynamic Programming
pattern.why: Only the last two prefix results are needed. Update them after comparing taking the current value with skipping it.
